title: EPFO Form 10C: Claiming Pension Benefits Explained
description: EPFO Form 10C is used to withdraw your Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) contributions or to obtain a Scheme Certificate. You can apply for a Scheme Certificate.

faq.q: What is the difference between Form 19 and Form 10C?
faq.a: Form 19 is used to withdraw your Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) accumulations, while Form 10C is specifically for claiming benefits under the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) – either withdrawal or a Scheme Certificate.

faq.q: Can I withdraw my full EPS amount?
faq.a: If you have completed less than 10 years of service, you can withdraw your accumulated EPS contributions as a lump sum. If you have 10 or more years of service, you cannot withdraw; you must apply for a Scheme Certificate.

faq.q: Is the amount received from Form 10C taxable?
faq.a: If your total service period is less than 5 years, the withdrawn EPS amount, along with EPF withdrawal, might be taxable as per income tax rules. If service is 5 years or more, it is generally tax-exempt.

faq.q: How long does it take for the Form 10C claim to be processed?
faq.a: Typically, online claims are processed within 15 to 30 days, provided all details are correct and verified by your employer and the EPFO. Offline claims might take longer.

faq.q: What if my Aadhaar is not linked to my UAN?
faq.a: You cannot submit an online claim without a linked and verified Aadhaar. You must first link your Aadhaar via the 'Manage -> KYC' section on the UAN Member Portal or through your employer.

faq.q: Can I submit Form 10C if my employer has closed down?
faq.a: Yes, you can still submit Form 10C. If applying offline, you may need to attest your claim form through a bank manager, gazetted officer, or magistrate if your previous employer is unavailable. Online submission requires prior employer verification of KYC.

faq.q: What is the purpose of a Scheme Certificate?
faq.a: A Scheme Certificate preserves your pensionable service if you have completed 10 or more years of service but are not yet 58. It allows you to combine your service periods across different employers to eventually claim a full pension at retirement.
